purpose: Auction & Surplus Scout source registry. Data, not code: a source can be re-routed (method/status) without a code change.

evidence.detail_page: HTTP 200, ~98 KB HTML; carries pick-up city/state/ZIP, bid count, current price, closing date/time and the buyer's-premium sentence
evidence.keyword_search: HTTP 200 for keyWord=generator (4 lots, incl. a 100 kW diesel generator)
evidence.search_page: HTTP 200, ~265 KB HTML for the all-Texas search; 25 auction cards per page

sources.name: Public Surplus
sources.reason: Public browse/search and lot detail pages serve full server-rendered HTML to a plain HTTP client (HTTP 200, no login, no JS required). Verified live 2026-11-17.
sources.texas_filter: region=all,tx search scope (server-side Texas filter); every grid card also carries a state badge that the parser verifies is TX.

entry_points: POST https://www.ppms.gov/gw/auction/ppms/api/v1/auctions?page=1&size=<n> with the public search body the gsaauctions.gov front end itself sends (states=[TX], auctionStatus=Active)

evidence.html_shell: GET https://gsaauctions.gov/ -> HTTP 200, 1,620 bytes, JS app shell only (no listings in HTML)
evidence.note: POST /api/v1/auctions/search (the other search route in the front-end bundle) timed out twice from this sandbox (25s and 45s) and is not used. GET /api/v1/auction-categories returns HTTP 401 for anonymous clients and is not used.
evidence.search: POST /api/v1/auctions?page=1&size=10 -> HTTP 200, totalElements=70, totalPages=7; page is 1-based (page=0 returns HTTP 500 'Page index must not be less than zero')

sources.name: GSA Auctions (PPMS)
sources.reason: The PPMS auction API behind gsaauctions.gov answers anonymous public search requests (the HTML site itself is a JS shell). Verified live 2026-11-17: stateCountList reported 70 active Texas auctions and the search POST returned them with city, current bid, bidder count and closing date.
sources.texas_filter: Server-side: the search body's states filter is [TX]; the parser also drops any returned lot whose location.state is not TX.

evidence.homepage: GET https://www.govplanet.com/ -> redirected to https://www.govplanet.eu/ (geo storefront), no Texas listing data extracted
evidence.search: GET /jsp/s/search.ips?sm=0&k=generator&mf=1 -> HTTP 202 with a 0-byte body (anti-bot challenge, no listing content)

sources.name: GovPlanet (IronPlanet / Ritchie Bros)
sources.reason: Anti-bot wall for plain HTTP clients: the search endpoint returns an empty challenge response and the .com homepage geo-redirects to the EU storefront. No public listing data is served to a plain client, so v1 ships an explicit stub. Next step is the BROWSER-AGENT route (an agent reading the public storefront like a visitor); v1 does not block on it.
sources.texas_filter: Not applicable in v1 (no plain-client access). A future browser route would filter the storefront's location facet to Texas.

evidence.legacy_page: GET https://www.tfc.texas.gov/divisions/supportserv/prog/statesurplus/ -> HTTP 200, 610 bytes, only a meta-refresh redirect to https://web.tfc.texas.gov
evidence.new_site: GET https://web.tfc.texas.gov/ and the surplus path on it -> HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai/edgesuite reference page)
evidence.surplustexas: GET https://surplustexas.gov/ -> connection closed by the remote end without a response

sources.name: Texas state surplus (Texas Facilities Commission)
sources.reason: No plain-client listing feed exists at TFC: the legacy surplus URL is only a redirect stub to the new TFC site, and the new site refuses plain HTTP clients (HTTP 403). Per TFC's own program documents, public sales happen at the Austin State Surplus Store and through online auctions run by contracted third-party auctioneers — TFC publishes no lot list of its own to pull. Texas state lots that surface on Public Surplus are already covered by the publicsurplus source.
sources.texas_filter: Program is Texas-only by definition; no machine-readable lot list is published by TFC itself.
